sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 25.01.2023 at about 5.00 p.m, when the petitioner was pushing a bicycle with tender coconut on B.M.Road, A.G.Circle and while crossing a road by observing all the traffic rules, at that time the rider of Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED-6212 came from Mysore side towards Bengaluru in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the petitioner's.
As a result of which he sustained grievous head injuries and after the accident he was shifted to Channapatna Government Hospital,
wherein he took treatment as inpatient and after necessary clinical examinations he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards treatment.
In spite of the treatment, he has not come to normal position and as such he has lost his income.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Honda Activa scooter.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the scooter and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence she was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 filed written statement denying the very issuance of insurance policy in respect of Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED-6212 and same is pending confirmation.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the offending scooter did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 25.01.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., near A.G. Circle, B.M.Road,
Channapatna Town, Ramanagara District due to actionable negligence of the rider of scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED-6212 ?

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 18 were marked on his behalf.
Further the petitioner has also examined the MRT of NIMHANS Hospital as PW.2 and through him got marked Ex.P.19 to 21 documents.
The Orthopedic Surgeon of Channapatna Government Hospital is examined as PW.3 and through him got marked Ex.P.22 & 23 documents.
The FDA at Channapatna Government Hospital is examined as PW.4 and through her got marked Ex.P.24.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 did not choose lead evidence.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of petitioner the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED-6112 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.6 being the spot mahazar and sketch categorically reveals that the petitioner was going in his Cycle from Channapatna towards Doddamaraluru side when he crossed the B.M.Road, A.G.Circle, Channapatna Town.

It is the Honda Activa scooter rider who had came from Mysore road towards Bengaluru Road with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and was without observing the crossing the road from others on the road and dashed to the petitioner.
It is further clearly shows that the spot of accident is a junction.
Ex. P5 & 6 spells in volumes as to the negligence on the part of the Honda Active scooter rider.
If the rider of scooter was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Further if the rider of the scooter drove his vehicle on the left side of the junction road by observing the on coming vehicles, then accident could have avoided.
Though the insurance company has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any evidence to this effect.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED- 6112.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

3 10. ISSUE NO.2 :

sentences.text:
As per the contents of the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
(1) Bleeding from left ear (2) CLW over left side of the scalp.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are simple in nature.

Ex.P9-Discharge Summaries discloses that the petitioner was taken treatment at NIMHANS Hospital from 25.01.2023 to 27.01.2023 and at Channapatna Government Hospital from 27.01.2023 to 31.02.2023 for a period of (8 days).
11.
The petitioner has deposed that on account of the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
So also the petitioner has not examined the doctor or produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact that he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances it cannot be accepted that he has suffered permanent disability.
Therefore he is not entitled for compensation under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
In this case the petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17 for having spent Rs.7,312/- towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
Anyhow because the petitioner has not proved that he has any kind of disability, compensation cannot be awarded under conventional heads.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the line of treatment and the medical expenses incurred by him, this tribunal is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the petitioner is awarded global compensation of Rs.80,000/-.

12. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
13. It is contended in para 7 of the written statement that respondent. No.1 has not issued any policy.

It is pertinent to note that IO has given Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.11 and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.12 wherein the owner of the offending motorcycle has admitted the involvement of the vehicle and in the reply she has clearly mentioned the motorcycle number as KA-42-ED-6212 and the issuance of insurance company name as Reliance Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., vide policy No.140522223750003338 and same is valid from 18.01.2022 to 17.01.2027.
Further the accident is occurred on 25.01.2023.
Further the police have also not filed charge sheet against the owner of the offending vehicle as the said vehicle was not having valid Insurance policy at the time of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-ED-6212 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

sentences.text:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.80,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
